text:
Sasha: perf-ci flagged a 95th p50-ish tail for SSE streaming on canary, blocking rollout :exclamation:
perf-ci-bot: [perf alert] canary: sse_stream_latency p95 +180ms vs baseline (job: ci/canary/stream-perf)
Sasha: top-level suspect is the api/proto-stream-change we merged this morning. It added an intermediate framing layer and modified toolcall serialization path.
Kevin: I ran a quick profile on the failing canary host. The hot path is in serialize_tool_response -> json.Marshal -> compress path. CPU ticks spike when streaming long tool outputs.
Priya: any chance batching heuristics changed? I saw a refactor in request_aggregator that bumped max_window_ms from 60 -> 120 in the PR.
Sasha: yes that change is in the same PR, they tried to smooth SSE flushes. Looks like it increases coalescing delay which pushes more work into bigger batches and forces heavier kernel selection for larger seq len.
Kevin: logs: ```
[2026-03-01T09:12:11Z] client=abc stream_chunk_flush delay=118ms batch_size=24 kv_cache_hit=false serialize_ms=42 tool_serialize_ms=90 total_ms=220
[2026-03-01T09:12:11Z] kernel_choice=matmul_large optimized=false
```
Priya: interesting: kv_cache_hit=false for those requests. Any change in kv cache key calc? The PR also adjusted toolcall cache key to include tool metadata. Could be invalidating prefixes.
Sasha: I instrumented prefix_kv when replicating: new key namespace added a random-ish metadata suffix due to a bug in metadata->string conversion. So cache hit rate dropped ~30% on canary.
Kevin: So we have a triple-whammy: increased flush window -> larger batches -> kernel autoselect chooses heavier kernels -> and worse KV caching -> no prefix reuse -> more token work -> higher serialization overhead for tool outputs.
Priya: reproduction steps I used: send a stream with intermittent toolcall outputs ~2-3KB each at 20ms intervals. On baseline (pre-PR) p95 ~120ms, on current canary p95 ~320ms.
Sasha: I started a bisect across commits in the PR branch. The exact commit that introduced the metadata->string formatting bug is 6f3a2d1. Reproduces locally.
Kevin: Can we hotfix by reverting the metadata string change and reduce the flush window back to 60ms? That should restore cache hits and reduce kernel escalation.
Priya: We should also consider a quick micro-optimization to short-circuit tool serialization for streaming responses: if tool output size > 1KB, stream it as raw bytes instead of JSON-ifying every chunk.
Sasha: For immediate rollout hold: revert commit 6f3a2d1 and the flush-window change in request_aggregator. I'll open a revert PR and tag @deploy-bot to hold canary.
deploy-bot: rollout hold applied to canary (reason: perf regression)
perf-ci-bot: CI perf job triggered a regression comment on PR #842: sse_stream_latency p95 +168ms
Kevin: I'm pushing a small patch to fix metadata->string (drop the metadata random suffix) and add a unit test for cache key stability.
Priya: I'll draft the streaming-path micro-optimization as a follow-up RFC; want to avoid changing protocols mid-rollout.
Sasha: Plan: 1) revert the two commits -> unblock canary, 2) run perf CI, 3) if green, continue rollout. 4) merge fix + unit test + RFC for streaming serialization path.
Kevin: Sounds good. I'll attach the flame graphs and the bisect output to the revert PR. Also adding a perf CI job variation that simulates small toolcall bursts.
Sasha: thanks. Quick note: add a telemetry gauge for kernel_choice per batch_size so we can detect autoselect escalations earlier.
Priya: ack, I'll make an issue and assign to runtime-observability. :+1: 
Sasha: closing loop — revert PR opened: https://git.redwood/infra/runtime/pull/891 Revert description: undo sse flush-window bump + metadata->string change causing kv key instability.
Kevin: will watch the perf CI run. If we still see a v-tail, we'll dig deeper into kernel selection heuristics.
Priya: nice find on the metadata suffix, that was subtle.
Sasha: thanks team. moving rollout hold -> will update when perf CI passes or we need to revert the revert. :white_check_mark:
